about: Expected case-runner failures on the one compiler (scripts/cases.mjs). Each entry names cases (an id relative to tests/, a glob, or a list), the lanes it covers (the --lanes syntax; omitted means all), why they fail, and the plan task that owns the fix (docs/migration/index.md). A failure not covered here fails the run; an entry that covers no failure any more is reported for removal. Recorded from the pre-M1 binary ~/lilscript-work/bin/pre-m1/lilscript (sha256 01c5e298...) on 2026-09-24: 29 failing cases, all harvested regressions; the 72 tests/cases programs and tests/modules pass on every lane.

entries.reason: Name-keyed host helper: the old route lowered the extern `objectHasOwn` to Object.hasOwn by its name; the one compiler gives extern names no meaning (dropped by design), so the program throws "objectHasOwn is not defined". The case's prelude must declare the binding (`globalThis.objectHasOwn = Object.hasOwn`).
entries.owner: M1.5 (the harvested case gets a declared binding; M10.2 owns the host catalog)

entries.reason: Refused at configuration load by design (D2): the case sets `public_aggregate_abi = "positional"`, and its host reads positional slots (`slot[0]`). Public aggregates are plain objects with named fields; the named siblings of these cases pass.
entries.owner: D2 (refused since M1.4; the case documents the refusal)

entries.reason: Refused at configuration load by design (D2): the cases set `public_aggregate_abi = "positional"` and their hosts read positional slots (`cache[0]`, `cache[1]`). The field-default order fault they also exposed was fixed in M1.9.
entries.owner: D2 (refused since M1.4; the cases document the refusal)

entries.reason: A struct value passed to an extern is refused: Unsupported "foreign value-struct storage adaptation".

The test expects the inferred wrapper name 'handle'. The rule is decided (architecture §10.2, plan M8.2 A1): a method's name is unobservable unless the contract keeps it (R6), so no lane owes 'handle'; here the struct's positional representation creates the function in an array slot, where JavaScript infers no name. The case asserts an unguaranteed name.
entries.owner: M10.14 (R6: rewrite the case to observe only what the reflected-set contract guarantees)

entries.reason: The test expects a non-empty wrapper name. The rule is decided (architecture §10.2, plan M8.2 A1): a method's name is unobservable unless the contract keeps it (R6). Production lanes let the method carry the name JavaScript infers and pass; formation-only lanes keep the callback's exact anonymous name, which the contract also allows.
entries.owner: M10.14 (R6: rewrite the case to observe only what the reflected-set contract guarantees)

entries.reason: Refused, not miscompiled: a struct union widened to JsValue, a generic function taking a struct ("generic product transport requires a complete private interface" on scripts) and a generic body that does not return its parameter ("generic product body requires closed value forwarding" on modules).
entries.owner: M1.9 (the struct-to-host family; the plan does not yet name this gap)

entries.reason: Native `Record<T>` is refused ("native source type", "native callable payload type").
